papers.title: A General Framework for Constrained Bayesian Optimization using Information-based Search
papers.abstract: We present an information-theoretic framework for solving global black-box optimization problems that also have black-box constraints. Of particular interest to us is to efficiently solve problems with decoupled constraints, in which subsets of the objective and constraint functions may be evaluated independently. For example, when the objective is evaluated on a CPU and the constraints are evaluated independently on a GPU. These problems require an acquisition function that can be separated into the contributions of the individual function evaluations. We develop one such acquisition function and call it Predictive Entropy Search with Constraints (PESC). PESC is an approximation to the expected information gain criterion and it compares favorably to alternative approaches based on improvement in several synthetic and real-world problems. In addition to this, we consider problems with a mix of functions that are fast and slow to evaluate. These problems require balancing the amount of time spent in the meta-computation of PESC and in the actual evaluation of the target objective. We take a bounded rationality approach and develop partial update for PESC which trades off accuracy against speed. We then propose a method for adaptively switching between the partial and full updates for PESC. This allows us to interpolate between versions of PESC that are efficient in terms of function evaluations and those that are efficient in terms of wall-clock time. Overall, we demonstrate that PESC is an effective algorithm that provides a promising direction towards a unified solution for constrained Bayesian optimization.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出的约束贝叶斯优化框架可迁移至生物力学设计中的代理模型辅助优化，但未直接应用于该领域。

summary_en.motivation: To efficiently solve global black-box optimization problems with black-box constraints, especially when functions are decoupled.
summary_en.method: Proposes an information-theoretic acquisition function called Predictive Entropy Search with Constraints (PESC) that approximates the expected information gain.
summary_en.result: PESC outperforms alternative improvement-based methods on synthetic and real-world problems, and can be extended with partial updates for wall-clock efficiency.
summary_en.validation: Validated on several synthetic and real-world benchmark optimization problems.

papers.title: Topological photonic crystal with equifrequency Weyl points
papers.abstract: Weyl points in three-dimensional photonic crystals behave as monopoles of Berry flux in momentum space. Here, based on general symmetry analysis, we show that a minimal number of four symmetry-related (consequently equifrequency) Weyl points can be realized in time-reversal invariant photonic crystals. We further propose an experimentally-feasible way to modify double-gyroid photonic crystals to realize four equifrequency Weyl points, which is explicitly confirmed by our first-principle photonic band-structure calculations. Remarkably, photonic crystals with equifrequency Weyl points are qualitatively advantageous in applications including angular selectivity, frequency selectivity, invisibility cloaking, and three dimensional imaging.

summary_zh.method: 基于对称性分析提出双陀螺光子晶体结构进行第一性原理计算
summary_zh.result: 实现了四个等频Weyl点并验证其优势

summary_en.motivation: Investigate the realization of equifrequency Weyl points in time-reversal invariant photonic crystals for novel optical functionalities.
summary_en.method: Conduct symmetry analysis and first-principle band-structure calculations on modified double-gyroid photonic crystals.
summary_en.result: Demonstrate four symmetry-related equifrequency Weyl points and predict advantages in angular/frequency selectivity, cloaking, and 3D imaging.
summary_en.validation: First-principle photonic band-structure calculations confirm the Weyl points.

papers.title: PECULIARITIES OF SINGLE TRACK FORMATION FROM TI6AL4V ALLOY AT DIFFERENT LASER POWER DENSITIES BY SELECTIVE LASER MELTING
papers.abstract: This paper describes the geometrical characteristics of single tracks manufactured by selective laser melting (SLM) at different laser powers (20-170 W) and scanning speeds (0.1-2.0 m/s). Simulation of temperature distribution during processing is carried out. A conclusion about the optimal process parameters and peculiarities of selective laser melting of Ti6Al4V alloy at low and high laser powers and scanning speeds is reached. The analysis of temperature fields creates opportunities to build parts with the desired properties by using SLM

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the geometrical characteristics of single tracks from Ti6Al4V alloy under varying laser power densities during selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Experimental observation of track geometry combined with finite element simulation of temperature distribution.
summary_en.result: Optimal process parameters were identified, and peculiarities at low and high laser powers were elucidated.
summary_en.validation: Validation was limited to simulation of temperature fields, without mechanical testing or experimental validation of part properties.
